qs.q: With a TAS of 115 kt the relative bearing on an ADF changes from 090° to 095° in 1½ min. The distance to the beacon is:
qs.ex: Time to station (min) = time for bearing change × 60 ÷ degrees changed = 1.5 × 60/5 = 18 min; distance = 115 × 18/60 = 34.5 NM.

qs.q: The ADF indicates a wing-tip bearing change of 5° in 5 min. TAS is 115 kt. The distance to the beacon is:
The ADF indicates a wing-tip bearing change of 5° in 1.5 min. The time to the beacon is:
With a TAS of 90 kt the relative bearing on an ADF changes from 090° to 100° in 2½ min. The distance and time to the beacon are:
The ADF indicates a wing-tip bearing change of 15° in 7.5 min. Fuel consumption 9.6 GPH, TAS 85 kt. Time, distance and fuel to the beacon are:
Maintaining a constant heading the ADF reading changes from 045° to 090° in 5 min. TAS 120 kt, fuel consumption 5 GPH. Time, distance and fuel to the beacon are:
qs.ex: A 45° change (045→090) means the distance flown equals the distance to the beacon (isosceles triangle): 120 kt × 5 min = 10 NM, 5 min.

qs.q: Maintaining a constant heading the ADF reading changes from 315° to 270° in 7 min. TAS 120 kt, fuel consumption 18 GPH. Time, distance and fuel to the beacon are:
At 60 NM from a station you travel approximately ____ NM for each degree of radial crossed.
During a climb from 1000 ft PA to 9000 ft PA, 50 air nautical miles are covered in 20 min. Track 090°, W/V 270/30 kt. Find the rate of climb and the ground distance covered.
qs.ex: TAS = 50 NAM ÷ 20 min = 150 kt; tailwind 30 → GS 180 → 60 NM. ROC = 8000/20 = 400 ft/min.

qs.q: An aircraft sets course at 4000 ft PA and climbs to 16 000 ft PA at 500 ft/min, mean wind 200/20 kt, constant RAS 130 kt (ISA −5 °C at 4000 ft and 16 000 ft). Time and distance in nil wind will be:
A to B is 30 NM and B to C 20 NM. ATA A 1010 UTC, ETA B 1030 UTC, ATA B 1027 UTC. What is the ETA at C?
qs.ex: A→B took 17 min for 30 NM (GS ≈ 106 kt); 20 NM more ≈ 11 min → 1038.

qs.q: X to Y is 30 NM and Y to Z 20 NM. ATA X 1420 UTC, ETA Y 1447 UTC, ATA Y 1450 UTC. What is the ETA at Z?
qs.ex: X→Y took 30 min for 30 NM (60 kt GS); 20 NM → 20 min → 1510.

qs.q: The chart MOCA is 8500 ft. OAT −20 °C at FL85. QNH at a station of elevation 4000 ft is 1003 hPa. What is the minimum pressure altitude to fly to respect the MOCA?
An aircraft at M0.84, FL330, SAT −48 °C, headwind component 52 kt. At 1338 UTC the controller requests the pilot to cross 030°W at 1500 UTC. Distance to go 570 NM. The reduced Mach number should be:
The planning chart gives 36 min and 157 NM (zero wind) to reach cruise level. What distance is covered with an average tailwind component of 60 kt?
qs.ex: 36 min at +60 kt adds 36 NM: 157 + 36 = 193 NM.

qs.q: An aeroplane flies at 380 kt from A to B and back to A. AB = 480 NM; headwind component 60 kt from A to B, wind constant. The flight time will be:
A sector is 450 NM, TAS 460 kt, tailwind component 50 kt. What is the still-air distance?
qs.ex: Air distance = ground distance × TAS/GS = 450 × 460/510 ≈ 406 NAM.

qs.q: A descent is planned from 7500 ft MSL to arrive at 1000 ft MSL 6 NM from a VORTAC, GS 156 kt, rate of descent 800 ft/min. The distance from the VORTAC when descent starts is:
qs.ex: Lose 6500 ft at 800 ft/min = 8.1 min; at 156 kt = 21.1 NM; plus 6 NM = 27.1 NM.

qs.q: An aircraft at FL370 must start descent 100 NM from a DME and cross the station at FL120. Mean GS 396 kt. The minimum rate of descent required is approximately:
qs.ex: Lose 25 000 ft over 100 NM at 396 kt (15.2 min) → ≈ 1650 ft/min.

qs.q: At 0422 an aircraft at FL370, GS 320 kt, is 185 NM direct to VOR X and must cross it at FL80. With a mean ROD of 1800 ft/min at a mean GS of 232 kt, the latest time to start descent is:
In zero wind, what distance is covered by an aircraft descending 15 000 ft at TAS 320 kt and 3000 ft/min?
What will be the rate of descent on a 7% glide slope at a groundspeed of 250 kt?
Aircraft height 2500 ft, ILS GP 3°. At approximately what distance from the threshold can you expect to capture the GP?
Wing-tip bearing change 10° in 8 min. Fuel consumption 11.8 GPH. Fuel required to reach the station (gallons):
qs.ex: Time to station = 8 × 60/10 = 48 min; fuel = 11.8 × 0.8 ≈ 9.4 gal.
